mode: 'and'/'was'/'were' after a sensory adjective describing food, clothing or scenery
'the' in superlative country or species claims: 'one of [the] lowest', 'has [the] highest'
mixed: 'or' in 'abandoned, [or] derelict', 'the most' before 'hated', 'the [distribution]' in statistics

summary: Fires on mid-clause function words in descriptive or superlative sentences (sensory description, 'one of the lowest'); not emotion-related.

mode: function word mid story sentence: 'rubbed them on [each]', 'they [did] not know how', 'friends [wouldn]'t'
punctuation or spacing at recipe and list step boundaries: '5[.] Season', 'salsa[,]', 'Bake for [ ]25 minutes'
mixed: comma after 'fruit', 'glaciers[ have]' in a report, 'including [psychological]' distress

summary: Fires on function words and punctuation inside ordinary narrative, recipe and report sentences, with no consistent content; not emotion-related.

mode: token after 'felt' or 'was' naming fear or anxiety: 'felt [scared]', 'Tip was [scared]', 'stress [can]'
'there' in the story opener 'Once upon a time, [there] was a little girl'

summary: Fires on the word after 'felt' or 'was' in fear, embarrassment or anxiety contexts, plus a weak story-opener mode; partly emotion-related.

mode: whitespace or brace tokens inside PHP and bash code, e.g. indent before an else-branch echo
'very' before a trait or feeling adjective: 'Tim was [very] impatient', 'She was [very] excited'
'so' after 'was', right before 'happy' or 'surprised'
opening quote mark or comma right after 'said' or 'said,' starting dialogue
period or spacing after a positive feeling line: 'so proud of herself[.]', 'so cool', 'so pleased'
'all' after 'They' starting a group reaction: 'They [all] ran over', 'They [all] thanked Jack'
'all' after 'was' in 'was all alone', 'all smiles', 'all covered in mud'
'was' after a character subject, right before 'so proud' or 'very proud'
sentence-opening subject pronoun or name after an action: '[He] shouted', '[She] closed her eyes', '[Anna] bent down'
mixed: 'What' opening a question, 'ran off [to]' find mom, 'flew [down]' for a closer look

summary: Fires on the token right before a predicate in simple children's stories ('was [so] happy', '[very] excited', '[all] alone', dialogue openers); emotion-related only in its happy and proud modes.

mode: 'play' or 'playing' after 'to', 'would', 'continued' or 'Let's' in children's stories
opening quote mark or comma right after 'said,' or 'said to Sam,' before dialogue
'and' right after a happy action: 'smiled [and] waved', 'laughed happily [and] laughed'
list number or first letter of a numbered or acrostic item: '5[.] Malala', '4.[ L]ululemon', '[N]ew beginnings'
mixed: 'extra [special]' comfort, 'leaves the [reader]', 'I love [you] both' after mom's praise

summary: Fires on verbs, dialogue openers and list tokens in children's narration and assistant-style text, with one smiling-and-laughing happy mode; only weakly emotion-related.

mode: gaze and face nouns: 'their [eyes] fixed', 'looked at each [other]', 'many sad [faces]'
'looked' right after a character subject: 'John [looked] up', 'She [looked] around'
sentence-opening pronoun or name after a stated fact: '[He] decided to jump', '[She] realized'
period ending an action sentence: 'looked around[.]', 'examined the chicken up close[.]'
mixed: period after 'said Jack', 'because it [was] empty', 'After' a few minutes

summary: Fires on gaze verbs, sentence-start pronouns and sentence-ending periods in narrated exploration scenes; not emotion-related.

mode: sentence-opening 'The' after an event: '[The] bunny was so happy', '[The] little girl thanked the policeman'
'was' after a character subject, right before 'so sad', 'so happy' or 'very ashamed'
'felt' after a character subject, right before 'sad', 'scared' or 'ashamed'
concrete place or object nouns after motion verbs: 'branch', 'bottom' of the hill, 'walked [home]'
name or pronoun starting the sentence after a dropped, broken or lost object: 'L[ily] was very sad'
period ending a loss or mistake sentence, right before 'He felt sad' or 'Timmy was very sad'
literary-review nouns: 'tracking [shots]', 'final [choice]', 'synth-heavy [soundtrack]', 'the [rush]' of power
'happy' or 'excited' right after 'was so' or 'was very': 'Timmy was so [happy]', 'Maya was so [excited]'
mixed: 'still' in 'but still tired', the closing mark in 'are you okay?', 'made me very [worried]'

summary: Fires on the word before a feeling or on the feeling word itself in children's story scenes ('felt', 'was so', period after a loss), strongest on sad, ashamed and scared contexts; clearly emotion-related.

mode: 'and' or 'she' right after a character's action, before 'smiled' or 'spun around'
pronoun after 'than' or 'as' in comparisons: 'than [he] hoped', 'as [she] thought', 'data [you] need'
mixed: 'I' starting a reply, colon in 'RxList[:]', period in numbered steps like 'Compare the first two elements... 3[.]'

summary: Fires on the function word or pronoun in a clause after a comparison or action, in narrative and how-to text; not emotion-related.
